data.name: Nimeshika
data.long_meaning: One who observes or perceives the truth.
data.numerology_meaning: The name Nimeshika is governed by the number 6. It represents the nurturing and caring aspect of life. It is a peaceful and loving name that is believed to bring harmony and balance in one's life. It is also associated with the goddess Lakshmi, who is the goddess of wealth and prosperity.

vedic_reference.note: Nimeshika is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Nimitta' (Observation) and 'Iksha' (Insight, Introspection).

data.cultural_impact: The name Nimeshika holds great significance in Hindu culture, as it signifies a keen observer or someone who has the ability to perceive the truth. In Hindu mythology, observing the truth is often seen as a valuable trait, as it leads to wisdom and knowledge. Nimeshika is also a common name for female deities, especially in Jainism, where she is revered as a Goddess of truth, knowledge, and perception.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nimeshika represents the inner journey of self-discovery and enlightenment. It signifies the importance of opening our eyes to the truth, both within ourselves and in the world around us. By Perceiving and understanding the true nature of reality, we can gain a deeper appreciation for life and the universe as a whole. In Hinduism, this internal search for truth is often referred to as "Jnana Yoga," or the path of knowledge and self-realization. Ultimately, the name Nimeshika serves as a reminder to always strive for knowledge, wisdom, and understanding, both in our daily lives and in our spiritual practices.

historical_references.reference: Nimeshika was a legendary queen of the Mauryan Empire, who is believed to have ruled around the 3rd century BC. She is known for her beauty, wisdom, and military prowess. According to legends, she was the wife of Emperor Ashoka and is considered one of the 16 queens of Ashoka mentioned in the Ashokan inscriptions.

Nimeshika is also referred to in the Indian epic Mahabharata as the name of a princess of the Vidarbha kingdom. She was the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandavas and the Kurus. Nimeshika is known for her loyalty towards her husband and her role in ensuring the peace between the two warring factions, the Pandavas and the Kurus.
